main_body: A small stall or gate: a blue-grey curved tile roof (rows 0-17) on two wooden posts, with a grey stone counter holding a blue water basin (rows 29-43).
top_band: Roof column x=16: a light grey-blue row at rows 1-2 (L=158 and 130), then a dark line at row 3. After that come vertical stripes at L=130 and L=104 that continue into the face. The top band is only about 2 rows. The counter column x=8 reads as a separate, clearly 3/4 part: a light rim at row 30, water at rows 31-34, and a rim at row 35.
evidence: The roof is the largest volume and the part the kind rule cares about. It is drawn as a front view: vertical tile stripes run from row 3 to row 15 with only a 2-row highlight along the top. There is no distinct lighter slope band, no front-edge line and no eave shadow beyond the bottom dark row. The posts and the dark gap between roof and counter are flat front-view elements. The counter is a correct 3/4 piece, with a 6-row top and basin and a 7-row front face. Under the mixed-drawings rule, the roof drawn in front elevation fails the whole drawing.

style.evidence: The roof has about 4-5 steps with a striped tile pattern, but it is regular and lacks per-tile scallops. The counter and posts are shallow: grey 3-step stone and orange posts of 2-3 tones. All dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), which gives the sticker outline, whereas the references use tinted outlines (1% and 33% neutral). The candidate has 9 colours per tile against 17 and 20 for the references, and 23 distinct colours against 38 and 40. That is far below both references, so it reads as thinner and flatter next to them.
